root_cause.component: The company's shipped networkd protection is in effect on no host. The platform role delivers Cilium's documented networkd override (50-cilium.conf, ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=no) to every host whose profile is cluster, but its handler only runs `networkctl reload`, and systemd-networkd reads networkd.conf.d only when it starts. The file was added to the platform repository with the change that enabled Cilium's L7 proxy; on every host that has it, networkd had started before the file arrived and was never restarted, so networkd runs with its defaults on every host, including the hosts that have the file
root_cause.description: Origin: the protection the company shipped never took effect, on any host: the platform role delivered the file after networkd had started and only ever runs `networkctl reload`, while networkd reads networkd.conf.d only when it starts. Not the origin: the fleet contract gap that leaves the three elastic hosts (us-work-01, us-work-02, eu-work-01) without the file. That gap is real, but it did not decide anything: hosts that have the file were exactly as unprotected. Which hosts were cut off was decided by rollout order: the canary zone and zone b received their package update and the re-configure that follows it before Cilium's L7 rules existed, so networkd had nothing to delete there; zone a, which is the elastic pool, received it after. Mechanism: networkd 249.11 with its default ManageForeignRoutingPolicyRules=yes deletes foreign policy rules when it re-configures a link. Trigger: a package update's scripts run daemon-reload, the netplan generator rewrites the .network file, and the platform role's next `networkctl reload` re-configures the link; networkd then deleted Cilium's rules (9, 10, 100) and the node was cut off. The systemd update's own restart of networkd came before the rules existed and before the file arrived, so it removed nothing and loaded nothing. Remaining risk: every host, with or without the file, loses Cilium's rules at its next package update followed by a role run; delivering the file to the elastic hosts changes nothing until networkd is restarted with the file in place; a restart on a host without the file removes the rules on the spot. Contributing defects (not the origin): the fleet contract gap for the elastic generation, two US gateway replicas that each forward every reading, a ledger unique by delivery attempt, and a writer that republishes partner rollups only for recent hours.
